info.title: Bookly API
info.summary: Booking, payment, studio and platform API for a marketplace of photographers in Kigali.
info.description:
The API behind the Bookly marketplace. It serves five kinds of caller:

- **The public**: anonymous visitors browsing photographers and their
  services, checking availability, booking a slot and paying its booking fee.
- **A booking's client**: no account needed; every client request carries a
  **capability token** in its path, emailed when the booking is confirmed.
- **A photographer**, in the studio under `/api/studio/*`: an
  `Authorization: Bearer` JWT from `POST /api/studio/auth/login`. Every
  studio route is scoped to the photographer the token names; an id of
  another photographer's row is a 404, exactly like an id that names nothing.
- **A platform admin**, in the console under `/api/platform/*`: a bearer
  JWT from `POST /api/platform/auth/login`.
- **A client with an account**, under `/api/account/*`: a bearer JWT from
  `POST /api/account/auth/login`, email verification or Google sign-in.
  Booking still needs no account.

Each signed-in area has its own login and its own token audience: a token
from one area is a `401` in every other, whatever its role claim says.

Read [the API conventions](/api/conventions) first: error shapes, the
400-versus-422 rule, time zones and money are the same on every operation.

This file is written by hand. A backend test (`src/openapi.test.ts`) fails
when a route exists without an operation here, or the other way round, and
validates real responses against these schemas.

get.description:
The public directory (marketplace-spec.md R6.1), 24 a page. Listed are
approved photographers whose subscription is `trialing`, `active` or
`past_due` (inside the grace), with at least one active package on an
active service. Pending, suspended and `expired` photographers never
appear. A `past_due` photographer is listed with `takingBookings: false`,
after every bookable one, and is left out whenever `date` is given.

**Date.** Kept are the photographers with at least one bookable start
that Kigali day for their shortest active package, exactly as
`GET /api/availability` would offer it: working hours (a dated override
wins), blocks, bookings and live holds, buffer and lead time. Accepted
from today (Kigali) to 365 days ahead.

Every parameter is optional and may appear once. An unknown parameter is
a 400. `Cache-Control: no-store`. Anonymous.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Highest `fromPriceRwf`, inclusive, whole RWF. Must not be below `min`.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: A Kigali date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, from today to 365 days ahead.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based; defaults to 1. A page past the end is an empty 200.

400.description:
Not the shape of a request: an unknown or repeated parameter, an
empty value, a slug or code of the wrong form, a number that is not
whole digits, a malformed date.

422.description:
Well-formed, but breaks a rule; `fields` names each: `category` (no
active category has that slug), `district` (no such district),
`min`/`max` (negative, past the int4 range, or `min > max`, which names
both), `date` (before today in Kigali, more than 365 days ahead, or a
year the engine cannot compute), `page` (below 1 or above 1000).

get.description: For the directory's filter bar (R6.1). Active categories only, in the platform's order. Anonymous.
For the directory's filter bar (R6.1). The five provinces in a fixed order (Kigali City first), each with its districts. Anonymous.

An XML sitemap (sitemaps.org 0.9) of the web app's crawlable pages
(marketplace-spec.md R6.6): `{WEB_ORIGIN}/`, `{WEB_ORIGIN}/photographers`
and `{WEB_ORIGIN}/p/{handle}` for every **bookable** photographer, each
profile with `lastmod` from its last update. Past-due, pending,
suspended and expired photographers are not listed. At most 50,000
URLs. Served at the API's root, not under `/api`: the web host rewrites
its own `/sitemap.xml` here. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`.
Anonymous.

The profile page behind `/p/{handle}` (marketplace-spec.md R6.2): the
profile, districts, categories, up to 24 portfolio images, the active
services each with its "from" price, the cancellation policy and the
contact details. Never the photographer's login email, status or
operating settings: `email` is the public contact address they chose, or
null. Text is verbatim: render it as plain text (R6.5). An unknown handle
and the handle of a photographer who is not listed -- pending, suspended,
or with an `expired` subscription -- are the same 404; the profile page
words it as "unavailable" (R5.5). A `past_due` photographer's profile is
served with `takingBookings: false`. Anonymous.

The photographer's active services, each with its active packages and the
add-ons it offers: its own, then those the photographer offers on every
service. Never another photographer's. A 404 for a handle that is unknown
or not listed (a `past_due` photographer's services are shown). Anonymous.

get.summary: One of a photographer's services by slug
get.description:
Slugs are unique per photographer, so the same slug under another handle is
another service. A 404 for an unknown or inactive slug, a slug only another
photographer has, and a handle that is unknown or not listed. Carries the
photographer's `takingBookings`. Anonymous.

200.description: The service, plus the booking-fee rate that applies to it.

post.description: The API's authority over money. The price is always computed from the catalogue, never from the body.

422.description:
A package or add-on the public cannot book; names the field. A package
whose photographer cannot be booked is refused as `packageId`, and an
add-on of another photographer -- even one they offer on every service
-- as `addonIds`.

get.summary: Bookable starts for a package in a month
get.description: Every Kigali date of the month with the slot starts a visitor may book for this package right now. `Cache-Control: no-store`. Anonymous.

422.description:
An unbookable package -- its photographer's included, answered exactly
as an unknown package -- or a month the engine cannot compute. The
month is the package's photographer's calendar alone.

post.summary: Create a booking and hold its slot
post.description:
Turns a chosen slot and a filled form into a `pending_payment` booking
holding its slot for the hold window. Anonymous. The returned
`checkoutToken` opens the booking's checkout.

409.description: The slot was claimed between the availability check and the insert.

422.description:
Something named cannot be booked, or the start is not currently offered
in the package's photographer's calendar. A package whose photographer
cannot be booked is `packageId`; another photographer's add-on is
`addonIds`.

429.description:
`too_many_holds`: the email already holds three unpaid slots, or
`rate_limited` (with `Retry-After`): too many requests from this IP or
email in the window.

post.summary: Email a client their booking links
post.description:
Sends one email with a fresh link for every current booking on the
address. The response is always `202` — a match, no match, or too many
requests are indistinguishable, so the endpoint cannot be used to learn
who has booked. Rate-limited per address and per IP.

202.description: Accepted. Whatever was found happens by email, to the address on the bookings.

422.description: Not an email address.

post.summary: Confirm a change of contact email
post.description:
Follows the link sent to the **new** address when a client asked to change
their booking's email. A POST, not a GET, so a mail scanner opening the
link cannot trigger the change. Unknown, expired, replaced and already-used
tokens are all a 404.

200.description: The booking now writes to the new address.

get.description:
The methods the pay pages may offer, in display order, and nothing else
(marketplace-spec.md R3.1). Each method is routed to its own provider:
MTN MoMo to MTN direct or Flutterwave (`MOMO_MTN_PROVIDER`), Airtel Money
always to Flutterwave. `PAYMENT_METHODS_ENABLED` may narrow the list, and
a method whose provider is not configured is never listed, so the list
may be empty. `card` is deferred and never listed. No provider is named:
which one collects a method is not the payer's concern.
`Cache-Control: no-store`. Anonymous.

get.summary: The checkout for a held booking
get.description: What the pay page shows. Addressed by the booking reference and its checkout token; a wrong token is a 404, as an unknown reference is. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.description:
Starts a booking-fee payment; the payer's phone is prompted through the
provider the chosen method routes to (R3.1). The amount is the booking's
frozen booking fee: an amount, provider or reference in the body is
ignored. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

201.description: The attempt was accepted; poll its `ourRef`.

409.description:
Nothing to start: `already_paid`, `hold_expired`, `nothing_to_pay`,
`photographer_unavailable` (the photographer can no longer be booked,
R3.4; nothing is charged), or `payment_in_progress` (an attempt still
waits — its `ourRef` is given).

422.description: A method not on offer (not enabled, its provider not configured, or `card`), or an unusable phone number.

502.description: The provider refused the request or could not be reached.

get.description:
The confirmation page polls this while a Mobile Money payment settles —
often 30 seconds or more. Addressed by the random `our_ref` the pay page
was handed; shows no contact details. `Cache-Control: no-store`. A
subscription payment's reference is a 404 here: the studio polls it at
`/api/studio/subscription/payments/{ourRef}`.

200.description: The payment and the booking it is for.

get.description: The booking the token addresses, and records the token's use. Any token that does not resolve is a 404.

post.description: Cancellable up to the shoot, and only on a confirmed booking. The booking fee is not refunded (it is non-refundable on a client cancellation).

409.description: Already cancelled, or the shoot has passed. Carries the booking as it stands.

post.description:
Stores the new address as pending and emails a confirmation link to it;
nothing changes until that link is followed, so a link-holder who is not
the client cannot redirect the booking's email without also owning the new
inbox. At most three requests a day per booking.

200.description: It is the address the booking already has; nothing to do.

202.description: A confirmation link is on its way to the new address.

409.description: A booking that no longer stands has no email to change.

422.description: Not an email address.

429.description:
`too_many_requests`: more than three requests today for this booking,
or `rate_limited` (with `Retry-After`): too many from this IP.

post.description:
Starts a session-fee payment for what the booking owes, through the
provider the chosen method routes to (R3.1). Only mounted when payments
are. The amount is computed server-side from the booking, never sent by
the client. Still payable when the photographer has been suspended since
the booking: existing bookings carry on (R5.5, T9.2).

201.description: The attempt was accepted; poll its `ourRef`.

409.description: Nothing owed, or an attempt already waiting (`payment_in_progress`, with its `ourRef`).

422.description: A method not on offer, or an unusable phone number.

502.description: The provider refused the request or could not be reached.

post.description:
Email and password for a photographer's studio. Returns a bearer JWT for
the `bookly-studio` audience, valid 8 hours, which no other area accepts.
Unknown email, wrong password, a locked account, an unverified address
and an account of another kind (a platform admin, a client) are one
answer — `401 invalid_credentials` — so none is disclosed; repeated
failures lock the account and email its holder. A pending or suspended
photographer can sign in. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

If the address is a photographer's login, a single-use reset link to
`/studio/reset-password`, valid 30 minutes, is emailed. The answer is
always `202`, whether or not it is, so the endpoint does not reveal which
addresses have accounts.

202.description: Accepted (sent only if the address is a photographer's login).

post.summary: Set a new password from a reset link
post.description: Consumes the emailed token and sets the new password, which revokes every token already issued. The token works once, and only here.

Creates a photographer's login, their studio (`pending` until a platform
admin approves it) and its settings in one transaction, emails a
verification link to `/studio/verify/<token>` (valid 24 hours), and tells
every platform admin there is an application to review. A pending
photographer can sign in once verified, and is not listed or bookable.

The answer is `202` whether or not the address already has an account,
so the endpoint does not reveal which do. A taken address gets, by
email only: a fresh verification link if it is an unverified photographer
login (its password is NOT changed), or an "you already have an account"
notice if its account is verified. A taken or reserved **handle** is
`409 handle_taken`, decided before the address is looked at: handles are
public.

409.description: The handle is taken, or reserved.

post.description:
Posted by the page the verification link opens (`/studio/verify/<token>`;
opening the link changes nothing). Requires the token AND the password
the account was created with: the token proves the inbox, the password
proves the person at it is the one who signed up, so a stranger who
signed up with someone else's address cannot have it verified for them.
Either being wrong is one answer, `400 invalid_verification`, and a wrong
password counts toward the account's lockout.

On success the address is verified, the link is spent, and the
caller is signed in: the response is a login's. Someone who never chose
the password the page asks for should use "Forgot password" instead: a
completed reset verifies the address and replaces the password.
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

If the address is a photographer's login whose address is still unverified, a new link
(valid 24 hours) replaces the old one and is emailed. Always `202`,
whether or not it is, so the endpoint does not reveal which addresses
have accounts or which are verified.

202.description: Accepted (sent only for an unverified login of this area).

200.description: The login and the studio it owns.

post.summary: Add a weekly rule or dated override

409.description: A rule already exists for that weekday or date.

422.description: An open day whose window does not open before it closes.

put.description: Replaces the whole row, so a rule can move between a weekday and a date.

409.description: A rule already exists for the target weekday or date.

422.description: An open day whose window does not open before it closes.

delete.description: Deleting a weekday rule closes that weekday; deleting an override restores the weekly rule for its date.

409.description: The range covers confirmed bookings; resend with `confirm: true` to save it anyway.

422.description: A range whose end is not after its start.

409.description: The range covers confirmed bookings; resend with `confirm: true`.

422.description: A range whose end is not after its start.

get.summary: The photographer's operating values and cancellation policy

patch.description:
Any subset of the six. Each is range-checked here, so a value out of
range is a 422 rather than a database error. Applies to bookings made
from now on; existing bookings keep the terms they were made under.

200.description: The settings as they now stand.

422.description: A value outside its range.

get.summary: Bookings, holds and blocks for a range

422.description: `to` before `from`, or a range over 62 days.

get.description:
The signed-in photographer's bookings only. Filtered by stage, status and
shoot date, searched by reference, name, email or phone (the booking's
own contact details), and paged by number with a total.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Repeatable. Kept for links made before stages existed.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based. Past the end, the last page is answered.

post.description: Keeps the booking, its reference, token and payments; moves the slot and its buffer to a free slot.

409.description: The slot is taken, or the booking cannot be rescheduled. Carries the booking.

422.description: A start the engine does not offer.

post.description: Releases the slot and marks the booking fee `refund_due` for a full refund. An optional reason is shown to the client.
Completing means paid. A booking that still owes money is a 409 `balance_due`.

409.description: Not in a state that can be completed, or money is still owed.

post.description: Issues a fresh token and invalidates the old one, then emails the new link.
Adds a catalogue add-on to a booking whose shoot has begun. The price is read from the catalogue, never sent.

422.description: An add-on the booking cannot take.

delete.description: Removes an add-on still removable (post-shoot, not yet paid for).

409.description: The add-on cannot be removed (not post-shoot, or already paid).

post.summary: Ask the client for the session fee
post.description:
Opens a session-fee request for what the booking owes and emails the
client. Only mounted when a payment provider is configured; without one
the route is a 404.

409.description: Not in a state to ask, nothing to ask for, or an attempt already in progress.

post.description:
Records cash the photographer was handed, up to what is owed. Refused
while an online payment may be in flight; it voids an open online request
so the same money cannot be taken twice, and emails nobody.

409.description: Not payable, nothing owed, more than is owed, or an online attempt in flight.

422.description: A malformed amount.

put.description: Sets the external photo link and its expiry on a completed booking. The link must be https.

expiresOn.description: Defaults to today plus the delivery-expiry setting.

422.description: A non-https or malformed link.

post.description: Emails the saved delivery link, optionally to another address for this one email. The booking's own contact email is not changed.

recipient.description: A one-off address; a mistyped one is a 422.

409.description: Not deliverable, or no link saved to send.

422.description: A mistyped recipient address.

post.summary: Add a note to the client
post.description: A plain-text note, emailed to the client unless `email` is false.

422.description: An empty or over-long note.

post.description:
Records that the photographer gave back **cash** he was handed (the
system never moves money). Needs the reference or note it was given back
with.

Cash only (Phase 4 refund decision). A payment made online sits in the
platform's account, so a platform admin refunds and records it
(`POST /api/platform/refunds/{paymentId}`); here it is
`409 refund_with_platform`, and the booking shows it with
`refundPendingWithPlatform`.

200.description: The booking the payment belongs to, as it now stands.

409.description:
`not_refundable`: the cash payment is not owed back.
`refund_with_platform`: the payment was made online; the platform refunds it.
The booking as it now stands is included.

422.description: A malformed reference or timestamp.

get.description: Every service (active or not) with its packages and own add-ons, and the add-ons offered on every service.

422.description: A value out of range, or a `serviceId` naming no service.
A value out of range, or a `serviceId` naming no service.

get.description:
What the photographer is owed and has been paid. The platform holds every
payment made online and pays it out by hand, with **no commission**; cash
the photographer was handed never appears here.

- A booking fee is payable as soon as it succeeds.
- A session fee is `pending` until the shoot has ended, then payable,
  unless the booking was cancelled.
- A refund before any payout voids the line; a refund after one adds a
  negative `reversal` that the next payout subtracts.

Each line carries its booking's id and reference, to link to it.

200.description: Totals, every line, and the payout history.

get.description: A draft being prepared or a paid payout of the signed-in photographer's. A cancelled draft, or another photographer's payout, is a 404.
Where payouts go now, or `null` if none has been saved. The page shows the transfer-fee banner (R4.5).

put.description:
Saves where payouts go (MoMo or bank). The previous method is retired, not
edited, so payouts already built keep naming the destination they were
built for (R4.1).

**Requires the current password.** Without it, or with the wrong one, the
answer is `403 invalid_password` and nothing changes; a wrong password
counts toward the account's sign-in lockout exactly like a failed login,
and once locked the answer is `403 password_locked` until the lock ends.
On success an `account_security_alert` email (payout method changed) goes
to the login address, and the platform's payout screen flags the change
for 72 hours.

Rate-limited per address (`429`).

403.description: The current password was missing or wrong (`invalid_password`), or the account is locked by failed attempts (`password_locked`).

get.description:
The subscription's status, the end of its current period, every period, any
payment in progress, the plan's prices for both intervals and the methods
on offer. `status` and `takingBookings` are computed from the clock, so they
are right even if the job that records them is late. `subscription` is null
for a photographer never approved.

post.summary: Pay for a month or a year
post.description:
Prompts the phone by Mobile Money for the platform's price of the chosen
plan. The amount is the server's: any amount in the body is ignored (T5.3).
When the payment succeeds (webhook or status lookup), a period of the plan
is added on top of the time already covered -- starting at the later of now
and the current period's end -- and a receipt is emailed (R5.3). Every
success adds its period, and none is ever refunded.

Any subscription status may pay, `expired` included. Refused with `409`:
`photographer_not_approved` (pending or suspended), `no_subscription`, and
`payment_in_progress` while another payment of the subscription still waits
on the payer (only one at a time). Rate-limited per address.

201.description: The phone is prompted. Poll the payment's `ourRef`.

409.description: Not approved, no subscription, or a payment already in progress.

502.description: The provider refused or could not be reached. The attempt is recorded as failed; try again.

get.description:
For the page to poll after a prompt: the payment, and the subscription as it
now stands. Another photographer's payment, a booking's payment and an
unknown reference are all a 404.

post.description:
Email and password for a platform admin. Returns a bearer JWT for the
`bookly-platform` audience, valid 8 hours, which no other area accepts.
Unknown email, wrong password, a locked account, an unverified address
and an account of another kind are one answer — `401 invalid_credentials`.
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

If the address is a platform admin's login, a single-use reset link to
`/platform/reset-password`, valid 30 minutes, is emailed. Always `202`.

202.description: Accepted (sent only if the address is a platform admin's login).

post.summary: Set a new password from a reset link
post.description: Consumes the emailed token and sets the new password, which revokes every token already issued. The token works once, and only here.

Posted by the page the verification link opens (`/platform/verify/<token>`;
opening the link changes nothing). Requires the token AND the password
the account was created with: the token proves the inbox, the password
proves the person at it is the one who signed up, so a stranger who
signed up with someone else's address cannot have it verified for them.
Either being wrong is one answer, `400 invalid_verification`, and a wrong
password counts toward the account's lockout.

On success the address is verified, the link is spent, and the
caller is signed in: the response is a login's. Someone who never chose
the password the page asks for should use "Forgot password" instead: a
completed reset verifies the address and replaces the password.
`Cache-Control: no-store`.

If the address is a platform admin's login whose address is still unverified, a new link
(valid 24 hours) replaces the old one and is emailed. Always `202`,
whether or not it is, so the endpoint does not reveal which addresses
have accounts or which are verified.

202.description: Accepted (sent only for an unverified login of this area).

get.description: Every photographer, newest first, or only those in one status.

post.description:
`pending` → `approved`: listed and bookable from now on. Records who
approved and when, and emails the photographer `photographer_approved`.
Idempotent: approving an approved photographer is a `200` that changes
nothing and sends nothing. A suspended photographer is reactivated, not
approved (`409`). Takes no body.

409.description: The photographer is suspended.

post.description:
`pending` or `approved` → `suspended`, with the reason the photographer
is emailed (`photographer_suspended`). The profile is hidden and new
bookings are refused; every existing booking carries on. Idempotent:
suspending a suspended photographer is a `200` that keeps the first
reason and sends nothing.

`suspended` → `approved`, or back to `pending` for one suspended before
ever being approved. Clears the suspension's date and reason. Idempotent:
reactivating a photographer who is not suspended is a `200` that changes
nothing. Takes no body.

200.description: The photographer as they now are.

get.description:
Every photographer whose payable balance is above nought, with their
current payout method. `methodChangedRecently` flags a destination saved
within the last 72 hours: redirecting payouts is what an account
takeover would aim for, so confirm it before sending money (R4.1).
Every payout, newest first, or only those in one status.

post.description:
Takes every line payable now for the photographer, totals it, and records
a `draft` for that amount to their current payout method. Then make the
transfer outside the app, and mark the draft paid with its reference.

Refused with `409` when the photographer has no payout method
(`no_payout_method`), already has a draft (`draft_exists`), or the total
is nought or less (`nothing_payable`: nothing is created, and the balance
carries forward to a later payout).

409.description: No draft was built.

post.description:
Records that the transfer was made: its MoMo or bank reference (required,
and used once across every payout), when, and by whom. Emails the
photographer `payout_sent`. Only a draft can be marked paid.

note.description: Platform-internal; not shown to the photographer.

409.description: The payout is not a draft (`not_draft`, with the payout as it stands), or the transfer reference is already recorded on another payout (`duplicate_transfer_reference`).

post.description:
Releases the draft's lines back to the photographer's balance, to be
taken by a later payout. Only a draft can be cancelled; who cancelled it
is recorded. Takes no body.

200.description: The payout, now cancelled, with no lines.

409.description: The payout is not a draft.

get.description:
Every refund of money paid online (MoMo through MTN or Flutterwave) the
platform has still to send, oldest first. The money is in the platform's
account, so the platform refunds it by hand and records it here. Two
kinds (`refundKind`):

- `full`: a payment owed back whole (`refund_due`). `refundAmountRwf` is
  the amount, less any overpaid part already returned. This includes a
  payment marked failed on our side (a session-fee ask voided for cash, or
  an attempt whose provider call failed) that the client then paid
  anyway, when none of it was due.
- `overpayment`: a session fee paid for more than the booking was worth.
  The payment stays `succeeded`, the photographer earned only what was
  due, and `refundAmountRwf` is the overpaid part.

A payment is listed once: a full refund covers its overpaid part, so a
payment that became `refund_due` after overpaying is listed only as
`full`. Cash is the photographer's to give back and is not listed.

post.description:
Records that money paid online was sent back by hand, with the reference
it went out with and the admin who recorded it. The system moves no
money. Records whichever refund is pending:

- `full`, when the payment is `refund_due`: it becomes `refunded`. This
  wins if both could apply, since a full refund covers the overpaid part.
- `overpayment`, when a succeeded session fee has an overpaid part not
  yet returned: the `overpayment_*` fields are set and the payment stays
  `succeeded`.

Refused with `409`: nothing pending (`not_refundable`), cash
(`cash_payment`: the photographer records that), a reference another
online refund of either kind already names (`duplicate_refund_reference`),
or a `refundKind` that is not what is pending (`refund_kind_mismatch`,
with `pending`: the list the admin acted on has changed).

reference.description: Unique across every online refund, full or overpayment.

refundKind.description: Optional. The kind the admin means to record, from the list they acted on.

409.description:
Cash (`cash_payment`), nothing owed back (`not_refundable`), a reference
already used (`duplicate_refund_reference`), or another kind pending
than the one named (`refund_kind_mismatch`). Nothing was written.

get.description: The checkout hold, the free trial, the plan's monthly and yearly prices, the grace days and the reminder days.

patch.description:
Saves any subset and answers every value as stored. What a change touches:
the hold, the next booking's; the trial, later approvals; the prices, the
next payment (one already started keeps its amount); the grace and reminder
days, every subscription at once. Each change is logged with who made it.

get.description: Every photographer's subscription, the soonest to end first, or only those in one status at the clock.

post.description:
Email and password for a client. Returns a bearer JWT for the
`bookly-account` audience, valid 7 days, which no other area accepts.
Unknown email, wrong password, a locked account, an unverified address,
a Google-only account and an account of another kind are one answer:
`401 invalid_credentials`. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

If the address is a client's login, a single-use reset link to
`/account/reset-password`, valid 30 minutes, is emailed. Always `202`.
A Google-only client may use it to add a password.

202.description: Accepted (sent only if the address is a client's login).

post.summary: Set a new password from a reset link
post.description:
Consumes the emailed token and sets the new password, which revokes
every token already issued. The token works once, and only here. A
completed reset also verifies the address (the link proved the inbox)
and links the bookings made under it.

Creates a client account and emails a verification link to
`/account/verify/<token>` (valid 24 hours). Bookings made under the
address are linked to the account only once it is verified, never at
signup: otherwise anyone could sign up with someone else's address and
see their bookings.

The answer is `202` whether or not the address already has an account.
A taken address gets, by email only, a fresh verification link if it is
an unverified client login (its password is NOT changed), or a "you
already have an account" notice if its account is verified.

Posted by the page the verification link opens (`/account/verify/<token>`;
opening the link changes nothing). Requires the token AND the password
the account was created with: the token proves the inbox, the password
proves the person at it is the one who signed up, so a stranger who
signed up with someone else's address cannot have it verified for them.
Either being wrong is one answer, `400 invalid_verification`, and a wrong
password counts toward the account's lockout.

On success the address is verified, the link is spent, the bookings made
under the address are linked to the account, and the caller is signed
in: the response is a login's. Someone who never chose the password the
page asks for should use "Forgot password" instead: a completed reset
verifies the address and replaces the password. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

If the address is a client's login whose address is still unverified, a
new link (valid 24 hours) replaces the old one and is emailed. Always
`202`, whether or not it is, so the endpoint does not reveal which
addresses have accounts or which are verified.

202.description: Accepted (sent only for an unverified login of this area).

get.description: Whether the login page shows "Continue with Google" (configured with `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`).

post.description:
Begins the OpenID Connect authorization code flow with PKCE (S256),
`state` and `nonce`. Returns Google's authorization URL, whose
`redirect_uri` is `<WEB_ORIGIN>/account/google/callback`, and the
state, which the page keeps in `sessionStorage` to compare on return.
The flow works once, for 10 minutes. No body. `404 not_found` when Google
sign-in is not configured. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Posted by `/account/google/callback` with the `code` and `state` Google
returned, once the page has checked the state against the one it kept.
The server consumes the flow, exchanges the code with its PKCE verifier,
verifies the id_token against Google's keys (signature, `iss`, `aud`,
`exp`, `nonce`) and requires a Google-verified address. Then it signs in
the client linked to this Google account; or links the client account
with this address (verifying it, and, if it was never verified,
discarding its password, which nobody proved was the owner's); or
creates a new client account with no password. The bookings made under
the address are linked. The response is a login's.

- `400 invalid_state`: unknown, expired or already used state. Start again.
- `400 google_sign_in_failed`: Google refused the code, the identity did
  not verify, or the account cannot sign in.
- `400 google_email_unverified`: Google has not verified the address.
- `409 account_conflict`: the address belongs to another kind of
  account, or to a client linked to another Google account. Word it
  generically.
- `404 not_found`: Google sign-in is not configured.

400.description: A malformed body, a bad state, or a refused identity.

409.description: The address belongs to an account that cannot sign in with Google.

post.description:
MTN signs nothing it sends, so the proof is in the URL: the path carries
our reference and `HMAC(our_ref)` keyed from `SESSION_SECRET`, and the
body's `externalId` must name the same payment. Only MTN is ever given
this URL. A body failing either check is stored, applied to nothing,
and answered 401.

put.description: Same as the POST callback; MTN may deliver either verb.

post.description:
Verified by the `flutterwave-signature` header, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw
body keyed by the dashboard's secret hash. A body whose signature does not
match is stored unverified, applied to nothing, and answered 401.

parameters.name: flutterwave-signature
parameters.description: Base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body.

studioBearer.description:
HS256 JWT from `POST /api/studio/auth/login`, audience `bookly-studio`,
valid 8 hours. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; never a cookie.
Refused once the password changes, the login is disabled or erased, or
its tokens are revoked; refused outside the studio.

platformBearer.description:
HS256 JWT from `POST /api/platform/auth/login`, audience
`bookly-platform`, valid 8 hours. Revoked like the studio's; refused
outside the platform console.

accountBearer.description:
HS256 JWT from `POST /api/account/auth/login`, `/verify` or
`/google/callback`, audience `bookly-account`, valid 7 days. Revoked
like the studio's (a Google-only client by a token revocation or by
adding a password); refused outside the account area.

KigaliDate.description: A calendar date in Africa/Kigali (UTC+2, no DST), `YYYY-MM-DD`. Years 0000–0099 are refused.

Rwf.description: Whole Rwandan francs. Money is never a float.

TakingBookings.description:
Whether the photographer can be booked right now (marketplace-spec.md
R5.4, R5.5). False while their subscription is `past_due`: they stay
listed, the page shows a "not taking bookings" notice, and their packages
answer the quote, the calendar and the booking form as an inactive package
does. An `expired` photographer is not listed at all.

DirectoryPhotographer.description:
One card of the directory (marketplace-spec.md R6.1). An allowlist: no id,
status, login, bio or settings.

fromPriceRwf.description: The cheapest **active** package of an **active** service. A photographer with none is not listed.

districts.description: Where they work, in the districts' fixed order (Kigali's first).

categories.description: What they shoot, active categories only, in the platform's order.

DirectoryPage.description:
One page of the directory: 24 cards at most, bookable photographers
first, then by `fromPriceRwf`, then by name (case-insensitive), then a
stable tiebreak, so pages never overlap or skip.

`total` is the exact number of matches across all pages, and is answered
**only without `date`**: under the date filter the availability engine
decides who stays, and it runs on the candidates up to the requested
page only, so no honest total exists. `hasMore` is always exact: without
a date `page * 24 < total`; with one, true only when a survivor beyond
this page was actually found.

total.description: Every match across all pages. Absent when `date` is given.

Error.description: Every error body. `error` is a stable, machine-readable code.

ValidationError.description:
A well-formed request breaking a rule (422). `fields` names the offending
fields so a form can mark them; values are never echoed back.

ProvinceDistricts.description: One of Rwanda's five provinces with its districts.

name.description: The province's English name, for display. A translated page may label it by `code` instead.

PublicCancellationPolicy.description:
The client cancellation terms the photographer offers new bookings, as
set now. A booking snapshots them when it is made, so a booking's own
pages state the booking's terms (`CancellationTerms`), not these.

cutoffHours.description: A client may cancel until this many hours before the shoot starts. 0 means any time before it.

bookingFeeRefundable.description: Whether a client's own cancellation refunds the booking fee. A photographer cancelling always refunds in full.

fromPriceRwf.description: The cheapest active package, whole RWF; null while the service has no active package.

PublicPhotographerDetail.description:
A photographer's profile page (marketplace-spec.md R6.2). An allowlist:
no id, no status, no login email, no operating settings. `email` is the
contact address the photographer chose to publish, or null -- never
their login; each contact field is null when not set.
`cancellationPolicy` is the one setting on it: the terms a new booking
would be made under.

**Every text field is returned verbatim** (`bio` included, markup and
all) and must be rendered as plain text, never as HTML or markdown
(R6.5, T6.4). Image URLs are `https://` only; render them with
`referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`.

bio.description: Plain text, verbatim. Line breaks are the photographer's own.

portfolio.description: At most 24, in the photographer's order.

services.description: The active services in catalogue order. Each one's packages and add-ons are at `/api/photographers/{handle}/services/{slug}`.

PublicService.description:
An active service with its active packages, and the active add-ons it
offers: its own first, then those its photographer offers on every
service, each in display order.

PublicServiceDetail.description: A service plus the booking-fee rate that applies to it, so a page can show a live quote.

bookingFeeRate.description: The service's own override if set, else its photographer's rate.

takingBookings.description: The photographer's, as on their profile, so the service page knows whether to open the slot picker.

QuoteRequest.description:
What to price. Any other key (a `totalRwf`, a `bookingFeeRwf`) is stripped
unread: the price always comes from the catalogue.

Quote.description:
The API's price for a basket. Only the booking fee is rounded (half-up, to
a whole franc); the session fee is the remainder, so the two always add
up to the total.

bookingFeeRwf.description:
Paid now to hold the slot. Whether a client's own cancellation refunds
it is the photographer's cancellation policy; by default it does not.

addons.description: In the order the service page lists them, whatever order they were selected in.

Instant.description: An ISO-8601 instant, always UTC in responses (`2026-10-14T07:00:00.000Z`).

days.description: Every Kigali date of the month, in order, each with the starts still bookable for this package right now.

OffsetInstant.description:
An ISO-8601 instant **with an explicit offset** (`2026-10-14T09:00:00+02:00`
or `…Z`). A bare local time is refused: it would be read in the server's zone.

BookingRequest.description:
Only ids and the form's text are read. Prices, statuses and any other key
are stripped unread: every amount comes from the catalogue.

startsAt.description: Must be one of the `starts` that `GET /api/availability` offers this package right now; anything else is a 422 naming `startsAt`.

email.description: Stored lowercased. A mistyped address is a 422, not a 400.

consent.description: Must be `true`. Recorded as `consent_at` (Law N° 058/2021). Omitted or false is a 422 naming `consent`.

BookingReference.description:
The booking's quotable reference: `BKY-`, the Kigali year and month it
was **made**, and five Crockford base-32 characters. Not a secret.

holdExpiresAt.description: When the slot is released if the booking fee has not been paid (the `holdMinutes` setting, 30 by default).

checkoutToken.description:
Opens this booking's checkout: the site's `/checkout/<reference>/<checkoutToken>`.
Present whenever payments are configured.

PaymentMethod.description:
`card` is reserved for the hosted card checkout, deferred (marketplace-spec.md
R3.2, 2026-10-17): it is never offered and a payment request naming it is a 422.

CancellationTerms.description:
The client cancellation policy the booking was made under: its
photographer's at that moment, kept on the booking, so a later edit of
the photographer's settings never changes it.

deadline.description:
The instant a client cancellation stops being accepted: the start
minus the photographer's cut-off, or the start itself when there is
none. Null on the client's booking page once nothing is left to
cancel (completed, no-show, expired or cancelled).

bookingFeeRefundable.description: Whether cancelling refunds the booking fee. A session fee already paid is always refunded.

waitingPayment.description: An attempt still waiting on the payer, if any; poll `GET /api/payments/{ourRef}`.

method.description: One of the methods on offer (`GET /api/payment-methods`); it decides which provider is prompted. Anything else is a 422.

phone.description: The number to prompt. Rwandan numbers may be local (`0788…`) or international (`+250788…`); an unusable number is a 422.

PaymentInProgress.description: An earlier attempt is still waiting on the payer's phone. Poll its `ourRef` instead.

PaymentNotStarted.description:
The provider refused the request (`rejected`: an unknown or unusable
number) or could not be reached in time (`unavailable`). The attempt is
recorded as `failed`; the payer may try again.

failure.description: Only for a `failed` payment. `unavailable` means the provider could not be reached; `declined` is everything else.

BookingStage.description:
The display stage derived from status and time (`booking/stage.ts`).
`needs_review` is admin-only: a client never sees it.

Totals.description:
Every amount a booking shows comes from these (`booking/totals.ts`).
A cancelled, expired or no-show booking owes nothing.

quotedTotalRwf.description: Package plus add-ons chosen at booking.

grandTotalRwf.description: The quoted total plus post-shoot add-ons.

collectedRwf.description: Succeeded payments, each for the part that was due (the amount less any overpaid part).

refundDueRwf.description:
Money owed back and not yet recorded as refunded: payments owed back
whole (less an overpaid part already returned), and overpaid parts of
succeeded payments not yet returned.

outstandingRwf.description: Still to pay; never below nought.

PaymentKind.description: The kinds a booking's payment can be. A subscription payment (Phase 5) is never one of a booking's.

ClientNotice.description: Something that happened to the booking since, newest first.

ClientBooking.description:
A booking as its own client sees it. Neither the booking's id nor the
token that reached it appears anywhere in it, and the contact email is
masked (`a•••••@example.com`).

pendingMaskedEmail.description: A requested change of email not yet confirmed from the new address, masked; null once its link lapses.

payments.description: Only money that moved or is owed back; abandoned attempts are left out.

canCancel.description: True only for a `confirmed` booking before its cancellation deadline (`cancellation.deadline`).

sessionFee.description: Present while a confirmed or completed booking still owes money.

delivery.description: Present once the photographer has sent the photos. `url` is null after the link expires (end of `expiresOn`, Kigali time).

ClientBookingConflict.description: The refusal, with the booking as it now stands.

PublicUser.description:
The only shape of a signed-in user that leaves the API, in every area. No
password hash, token hashes, Google subject, token version, lockout state
or role.

token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, to this area only. Keep it in memory or `sessionStorage`, never `localStorage`.

handle.description:
The public profile is `/p/<handle>`. Trimmed and lowercased first,
then 3-30 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, not starting or ending
with `-` (the database's `photographer_handle_format`). Reserved
names (`admin`, `api`, `p`, `studio`, `platform`, `account`,
`photographers`, `services`, `checkout`, `booking`, `my-booking`,
`email-confirm`, `login`, `signup`, `help`, `docs`, `static`,
`assets`) are refused like a taken handle.

SignupAccepted.description: Always this, whether or not the address already had an account.

VerifyRequest.description:
The token from the emailed link (`/{area}/verify/<token>`) and the
password the account was created with. Both are required: the token
proves the inbox, the password proves the person at it signed up.

PhotographerStatus.description:
`pending` until a platform admin approves; `approved` is listed and
bookable; `suspended` is hidden and takes no new bookings, but keeps every
booking it already has.

photographer.description: The studio the login owns. Its `status` drives the pending or suspended banner.

WorkingHours.description: A weekly rule (`weekday` set) or a one-date override (`effectiveDate` set), never both.

WorkingHoursWrite.description:
Exactly one of `weekday` and `effectiveDate`: both or neither is a 400.
An open day needs `opensMinute` before `closesMinute` (else 422). One rule
per weekday and one override per date: a duplicate is 409 `working_hours_exists`.

endsAt.description: Exclusive. A whole-day block ends at the Kigali midnight after its last day.

reason.description: Private to the admin. No public endpoint ever returns it.

BlockWrite.description:
Whole days as inclusive Kigali dates, or a time range as instants with an
offset. Overlapping a `confirmed` booking is a 409 naming it unless
`confirm: true` is sent; the booking is never cancelled by a block.

BlockConflict.description: The block would cover confirmed bookings. Resend with `confirm: true` to save it anyway.

Settings.description:
The signed-in photographer's own operating values and client cancellation
policy. The checkout hold is the platform's and is not here. A booking
keeps the buffer, fee rate and cancellation policy it was made under, so
a change applies to new bookings only.

bookingFeeRate.description: Share of the total paid up front (0.4 by default). At most three decimal places.

minLeadTimeMinutes.description: Minimum notice before a bookable start (120 by default).

bufferMinutes.description: Gap reserved after every shoot (30 by default).

clientCancelCutoffHours.description: A client may cancel until this many hours before the shoot. 0 (the default) means any time before it.

bookingFeeRefundableOnClientCancel.description: Whether a client's own cancellation refunds the booking fee (false by default). A photographer cancelling always refunds it.

SettingsPatch.description:
Any subset of the six values. An unknown key is a 400, so a misspelt field
never silently saves nothing; that includes `holdMinutes`, which is the
platform's now.

bookings.description: What occupies time. `pending_payment` appears only while its hold is live; cancelled and expired bookings are left out.

conflictsWithBlock.description: The session overlaps a block that was saved over it anyway.

bookings.description: Newest shoot first (start, then id, descending).

total.description: Every booking the filter matches, across all pages.

page.description: The page answered; a page past the end answers the last one.

note.description: What was typed with a cash payment.

canRecordRefund.description: A cash payment owed back, which the photographer records once he has given it back (`POST /api/studio/payments/{id}/refund`). Always false for a payment made online.

refundPendingWithPlatform.description:
A payment made online that is owed back. The money is in the platform's
account, so a platform admin refunds the client and records it; the
studio shows it as pending with the platform (Phase 4 refund decision).

overpaidRwf.description:
The part of a session fee paid online over what the booking was worth
(Phase 4 overpayment decision); 0 when it was not overpaid. The payment
stays `succeeded`; its earning, and the booking's totals, count only
`amountRwf - overpaidRwf`.

overpaymentRefundPendingWithPlatform.description:
That overpaid part is still to go back to the client. The money is in
the platform's account, so the platform returns it and records it; there
is nothing for the photographer to do. False once the platform records
it, and false once the whole payment is owed back (a full refund covers it).

overpaymentRefundedAt.description: When the platform returned the overpaid part.

overpaymentRefundReference.description: The reference it went back with.

AdminBooking.description:
One of the signed-in photographer's bookings. The client's details are the
booking's own snapshot (`contact`); the platform's shared client record is
never shown to a photographer.

contact.description: The contact details this booking was made with (its own snapshot).

originalStartsAt.description: Set on the first reschedule only.

access.description: The client's link. The token itself is never stored, so it cannot be shown.

messages.description: Every message queued for this booking, with its delivery state.

notes.description: Notes to the client, newest first. Deleted notes are gone.

actions.description: What may be done to the booking now. The API checks again on every action.

canEditAddons.description: Confirmed, and the shoot has begun.

AdminBookingConflict.description:
The action was refused. `error` says why; `booking` is the booking as it
now stands, so a screen acting on a stale view can show what is true.

bookingFeeRateOverride.description: Null means the global booking-fee rate applies.

serviceId.description: Null means offered on every service.

services.description: Every service, active or not, with all its packages and its own add-ons.

sharedAddons.description: Add-ons offered on every service (`serviceId` null).

ServiceWrite.description:
Create requires `slug` and `nameEn`; an update sends any subset. Blank
optional text is stored as null. Unknown keys are a 400.

slug.description: Lowercase words joined by single hyphens. Unique; a taken slug is 409 `slug_taken`.

coverImageUrl.description: A pasted link to an image hosted elsewhere. Must be `https:`; `http:` is a 422.

bookingFeeRateOverride.description: At most three decimal places. Null uses the global rate.

PackageWrite.description: Create requires `serviceId`, `nameEn`, `priceRwf`, `photoCount` and `durationMinutes`; `serviceId` cannot be changed later.

serviceId.description: Create only. A service that does not exist is a 422 naming `serviceId`.

PackageSaved.description:
The saved package, and a warning when it is longer than every open day
(spec §6.8): saving is allowed, but no client will ever see a slot for it.

longestWindow.description: The longest open window, in minutes after Kigali midnight; null with no open day at all.

AddonWrite.description: Create requires `serviceId` (null for every service), `nameEn` and `priceRwf`; `serviceId` cannot be changed later.

PayoutItemState.description:
`pending`: succeeded but not payable yet (a session fee before its shoot
has ended). `payable`: payable now, in no payout. `in_draft`: in a payout
being prepared. `paid`: in a payout marked paid. `voided`: refunded before
any payout, so it no longer counts.

PayoutItem.description:
One line of what the photographer is owed: an `earning` (a succeeded booking
or session fee paid online, its full amount: no commission) or a
`reversal` (the negative of an earning already paid out, after its payment
was refunded). Cash never has a line.

amountRwf.description: Positive for an earning, negative for a reversal.

booking.description: The booking the line is for. `id` opens it in the studio.

PayoutMethod.description:
Where the photographer is paid. Immutable: saving a new one retires this
row and creates another, so `id` changes on every save.

accountName.description: The name the account is registered to.

transferReference.description: The MoMo or bank transaction id

payoutMethod.description: The destination it was sent, or is being sent, to.

totals.description: Sums of the lines in each state. `payableRwf` may be nought or negative when reversals outweigh new earnings.

items.description: Every line, voided ones included, newest first.

payouts.description: The draft being prepared, if any, and every paid payout, newest first. Cancelled drafts are not shown.

payoutMethod.description: The current destination, or null if none has been saved.

PayoutMethodRequest.description:
One of two shapes, by `kind`; a field of the other shape is a `400`.
`currentPassword` is the account's password: without it, or wrong, the
change is a `403`.

momoNumber.description:
A Rwandan mobile number, typed any usual way (`0788 123 456`,
`+250 788 123 456`); stored as E.164. It must be on the network's
own prefixes (MTN 078/079, Airtel 072/073), or it is a `422`.

bankAccountNumber.description: Letters, digits, spaces and dashes, with at least one digit.

SubscriptionStatus.description:
`trialing` or `active` while the current period runs; `past_due` from its
end until the grace days are over (listed, not bookable); then `expired`
(hidden). Computed from the clock, so it is right even when the job that
records it runs late (R5.4).

SubscriptionPeriod.description:
One stretch of time the subscription covers: the free trial, or a paid month
or year. A paid period starts where the time already covered ends, so
paying early adds time on top (R5.3).

priceRwf.description: What was paid; 0 for the trial.

paidAt.description: When its payment succeeded; null for the trial.

SubscriptionPayment.description:
One subscription payment as the photographer may see it. `failure` says
why a failed one failed, as the payer may be told it: `declined` (turned
down, timed out on the phone, an unknown number) or `unavailable` (the
provider could not be reached). The recorded reason stays internal.

currentPeriodEndsAt.description: The end of the latest period, paid or trial.

graceEndsAt.description: When a lapsed subscription becomes `expired` and the profile is hidden.

takingBookings.description: Whether clients can book the photographer now (approved, and the period still running).

currentPeriod.description: The period now falls in; null once the last one has ended.

paymentInProgress.description: A payment still waiting on the payer, which blocks starting another; null if none.

subscription.description: Null before approval (the subscription and its trial start then, R5.1).

prices.description: The plan's prices, whole RWF, set by the platform.

methods.description: The methods on offer, MoMo only while cards are deferred. Empty when no payment provider is configured.

SubscriptionPayRequest.description:
The plan and how to pay. The amount is never the request's: any other key
(an `amountRwf`, a `status`) is ignored, and the platform's price for the
plan is charged (T5.3).

method.description: One of `methods` from the subscription page; anything else is a 422.

phone.description: The MoMo number to prompt, local (`0788…`) or international (`+250788…`). An unusable number is a 422.

approvedByUserId.description: The platform admin who approved them.

suspendedAt.description: When the current suspension began. Cleared on reactivation.

suspensionReason.description: The reason given for the current suspension, as emailed to the photographer.

PlatformPayoutMethod.description: A payout method as the platform sees it, with when it was replaced.

retiredAt.description: When the photographer replaced it; null while current.

due.description: Photographers whose payable balance is above nought, largest first.

payoutMethod.description: The current destination; null when none is saved (a draft cannot be built).

methodChangedRecently.description: The destination was saved within the last 72 hours (R4.1). A takeover would aim here; confirm with the photographer before sending.

draftPayoutId.description: A draft already being prepared, which must be paid or cancelled before another is built.

amountRwf.description: The items' total when the draft was built.

itemCount.description: Nought once a draft is cancelled

payoutMethod.description: The destination the draft was built for.

payoutMethodIsCurrent.description: False once the photographer has saved another destination since the draft was built. Check before transferring.

methodChangedRecently.description: The photographer's current destination was saved within the last 72 hours (R4.1).

note.description: What the admin typed when marking it paid. Platform-internal.

BuildRefused.description:
`no_payout_method`: the photographer has no destination saved.
`draft_exists`: a draft is already being prepared (`payoutId` names it).
`nothing_payable`: the payable total is nought or less (`payableRwf`);
nothing was created and the balance carries forward.

PayoutNotDraft.description: Only a draft can be marked paid or cancelled. The payout as it now stands.

RefundKind.description:
`full`: the payment is owed back whole (`refund_due`). `overpayment`: a
session fee paid online for more than the booking was worth; it stays
`succeeded`, and only the overpaid part goes back (Phase 4 overpayment
decision). A payment is listed once: a full refund covers its overpaid part.

refundAmountRwf.description:
What to send back. `full`: the whole amount, less an overpaid part the
platform already returned. `overpayment`: the overpaid part.

overpaidRwf.description: The payment's overpaid part, returned or not; 0 when it was not overpaid.

status.description: A full refund leaves the payment `refunded`; an overpayment refund leaves it `succeeded`.

refundedAt.description: When that refund was sent (`refunded_at`, or `overpayment_refunded_at`).

holdMinutes.description: The checkout hold. At most 60, the reconciler's window.

trialDays.description: The free trial approval starts. A change applies to later approvals.

subscriptionGraceDays.description: Days of `past_due` after a period ends, before `expired`.

subscriptionReminderDays.description: Days before a period ends that a reminder goes out, largest first. Empty sends none.

PlatformSettingsUpdate.description: Any subset of the settings. An unknown key is a 400; a value outside its bounds a 422 naming it.

AuthProviders.description: Which sign-in methods the account login page offers besides a password.

authorizationUrl.description: Google's authorization page. Send the browser there.

state.description:
Keep it in `sessionStorage` and compare it with the `state` Google
returns to `/account/google/callback` before posting the callback.
Works once, for 10 minutes.

AccountUser.description: A client's own view of their account. Still an allowlist.

Handle.name: handle
Handle.description:
A photographer's handle, as in `/p/{handle}`: lowercase letters, digits
and hyphens, 3 to 30 characters. Anything else is a 404, as an unknown
handle is.

AccessToken.name: token
AccessToken.description:
The booking's **access token**, from its confirmation email or a resend:
256 random bits, base64url. It is the client's whole identity, so treat
the URL as a secret. Unknown, expired (365 days) and superseded tokens
are all a 404.

CheckoutToken.name: token
CheckoutToken.description:
The checkout token returned when the booking was created: an HMAC of the
reference, 43 base64url characters. Good only for paying the booking fee
while the hold lasts.

OurRef.name: ourRef
OurRef.description: Our id for one payment attempt, returned when it was started.

NotFound.description:
Nothing there. For a capability token this is also the answer for an
expired, superseded or malformed token: never 403, which would confirm
that a booking exists. On a studio route it is also the answer for an id
that belongs to another photographer.

BadRequest.description:
Not the shape of a request: invalid JSON, a wrong type, an unknown or
missing key, a malformed id or date.

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests from this address (or, for bookings, this email) in the
window. Nothing was done. `Retry-After` gives the seconds to wait.

InvalidCredentials.description:
Invalid credentials. One answer for an unknown email, a wrong password, a
locked account, an unverified address and an account of another kind:
none is disclosed.

ResetConfirmRefused.description: A malformed body, or an invalid or expired token.

ValidationFailed.description: Well-formed, but a value breaks a rule. Names the fields.

VerifyRefused.description:
A malformed body (`invalid_request`), or one answer
(`invalid_verification`) for an unknown, expired or used token, a wrong
password, a locked account and a login since disabled: none is
disclosed. A wrong password counts toward the account's lockout.

Unauthorized.description:
No valid token for this area. The `WWW-Authenticate` header says which:
`Bearer realm="bookly-studio"` (or `bookly-platform`, `bookly-account`) for no token,
`…, error="invalid_token"` for a refused one: expired, tampered, issued
for another area, issued before a password change or a revocation, or
for a login since disabled.

booking.description: The booking as it now stands.

conflict.description: The action was refused; the booking as it stands is included.

slugTaken.description: The slug is already in use.

invalid.description: A well-formed value outside its rules.

inUse.description: A booking or another row still references this; it was not deleted.

package.description: The package, with a warning when it is longer than every open day.

received.description: The delivery is on record, applied or ignored.

invalidSignature.description: The signature did not verify. The delivery is stored unverified and changed nothing (T3.3).

failed.description: Processing failed; the provider should retry.
